data_output.description: data.py load() continues to return split rows in canonical source order. encode(splits) continues to return (encoded, dimension); each encoded split is (features, labels, users), where features is an int32 matrix with columns [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday], labels is float32, and users is U32. The three added fields use only train-fitted vocabularies with one unknown bucket each.

model_input.description: model.py receives the encoded int32 feature matrix and the total five-field vocabulary dimension. Model.logits must remain bias plus the sum of the five indexed weights for each row; no interactions, loss, optimizer, or schedule changes are permitted.

feature_engineer.objective: Extend the neutral ID feature encoding with exactly the request_context group {tab, hour, weekday} while preserving the existing data interface and canonical row order.
required_changes: In data.py, read the exact raw columns tab, hourmin, and date from each log_standard_4_08_to_4_21_pure.csv and log_standard_4_22_to_5_08_pure.csv row; do not introduce aliases or read excluded fields.
Derive hour exactly as integer floor(numeric hourmin / 100), constrained to 0..23.
Derive weekday exactly as the calendar weekday of the YYYYMMDD date, with Monday=0 through Sunday=6.
Retain user_id and video_id as the first two encoded feature fields and add tab, hour, and weekday as three additional categorical fields, for a five-column encoded feature matrix.
Fit all five vocabularies on the training split only, allocate one unknown bucket per field, and preserve the existing offset-based single-vector indexing scheme.
Keep encode(splits) returning (encoded, dimension), with each encoded split retaining the existing (features, labels, users) tuple shape so train.py remains compatible.

Preserve source filtering and row order: split rows must remain in the order produced by load(), and validation features, labels, and users must remain aligned in canonical validation source-row order.
preserve: The LABEL, SPLITS, input filenames, train-only vocabulary fitting, unknown-bucket behavior, int32 feature dtype, float32 labels, and U32 user IDs.

The neutral additive architecture: features are independent categorical indices consumed by Model.logits as a sum of per-index weights; do not add interactions, embeddings, baselines, profile aggregates, or any other feature group.
The existing BCE training objective, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and configuration values; do not modify model.py, train.py, or config.json.
coordination_notes: The resulting model input is an int32 matrix of shape (N, 5), with dimension equal to the sum of the five train-fitted vocabulary dimensions including unknown buckets.
The fixed trainer continues to receive the unchanged three-element encoded tuple and must emit only row_ids and scores; no ground-truth labels may be written to predictions_valid.npz.
Use only the canonical schema names and recipes: raw tab; raw hourmin for hour=floor(numeric hourmin/100) constrained to 0..23; raw date for Monday=0..Sunday=6 weekday.

reasoning: Only feature_engineer is activated because model.py already implements a dimension-agnostic additive scorer and the existing trainer already writes exactly row_ids and scores without changing configuration. The data change is limited to the request_context group, uses training-only vocabularies, and preserves the existing train.py interface and canonical validation order.
